subject: Avante Health — Dedicated GPU pool onboarding readiness & burst policy questions
body:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Rajesh Patel <r.patel@avantehealth.com>, Anika Bose <anika.bose@avantehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Avante Health — Dedicated GPU pool onboarding readiness & burst policy questions

Hi Rajesh / Anika —

Great to get moving on the Dedicated pool for Avante (AVN-4721). I attached a first-pass sizing spreadsheet and the current MSA redline PDF for your legal/procurement review. Before we spin up the pool, two quick asks so we can produce a firm implementation plan and estimated turn-up timeline: 

1) Region preference (us-east-1 / us-west-2 / eu-west-1) — you mentioned US-first in the call; please confirm a region and whether you require data residency in a specific region.
2) Expected steady-state concurrency and peak burst (qps or concurrent requests, or rough monthly token throughput) — the sizing sheet has scenarios; tell us which row most closely matches your expected load.
3) Autoscale & burst policy intent — do you want tight SLOs for latency (e.g., p95 < 120ms) that trade cost for headroom, or strict cost-control with defined cold-start tolerances?
4) Network/Firewall contacts — we’ll need an L3/NetOps contact for egress rules and peering.

Next steps after your answers: Ben (ops) will validate hardware footprint and burst policy, Kim (implementation) will schedule the kickoff and share the mutual action plan, and I’ll coordinate DocuSign + procurement items.

Attachments: avante_sizing_estimate_v1.xlsx, MSA_redline_20270401.pdf, network_requirements_v1.docx

Thanks — talk soon,

—
Tessa Morgan
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
Email: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0199

This thread is the kickoff for Dedicated capacity onboarding (GPU pool provisioning, autoscaling/burst policies, regional capacity selection).

Hi Tessa —

Thanks for the clear list. A few quick responses: 
- Region: us-east-1 is our preferred region for initial rollout due to data routing and supplier agreements. We may expand later.
- Load: initial pilot will be modest — ~30 concurrent requests at peak (low tens of QPS). Production target in 3 months is 300 concurrent / ~1.2M tokens/day. The sizing sheet row "Pilot - Medium" looks closest.
- Autoscale/burst: we need predictable latency for our clinical inference (p95 < 150ms). Cost is important but not at the expense of patient experience. We are comfortable with a small reserved footprint and burst capacity during spikes.
- Compliance: Avante is HIPAA-covered; we will need to confirm DPA and SOC2 artifacts.

Looping in procurement contact for contract redlines.

Thanks,
Rajesh

Thanks — copying Ben (ops) for sizing and burst confirmation and Kim (implementation lead) for the SOW / action plan. 

Ben / Kim — quick internal notes (please reply-all with confirmations):
- Region: us-east-1 (confirmed by customer).
- Pilot footprint ask: reserve a minimal steady-state of 4xA100-class GPUs (pilot), with autoscale up to 8 for production targets; allow a short-duration burst to 12 with preapproved guardrails. We should call out warm prefix caching and batching guidance to meet p95 goals.
- Network: customer requires private peering / VPC and egress rules; see attached network_requirements_v1.docx — earliest cutover requires netops coordination 5 business days prior to activation.
- Compliance artifacts: please attach SOC 2 evidence and BAA draft to the SOW package.

Kim: can you draft a 6-8 week mutual action plan (pilot -> production) and a 60-minute kickoff invite next week? Ben: confirm whether 4xA100 is sufficient for the pilot with our runtime (opt kernels + quantization).

I’ll prep the DocuSign packet once we have the SOW and the procurement asks addressed.

—
Tessa

Subject: Re: Avante Health — Dedicated GPU pool onboarding readiness & burst policy questions

Tessa / team —

Quick ops confirmation:
- Pilot hardware: 4 x A100 40GB should be fine for the pilot assumptions (30 concurrent / pilot load), assuming model quantization to int8 for lower memory footprint.
- Autoscale: recommend target pool of 4 reserve; autoscale min=4, target=6 under average burst, max=12 for emergency burst (policy: scale-up threshold at 70% avg GPU util over 30s, cool-down 120s).
- Burst policy: allow short, policy-controlled burst (<=10 minutes) to max=12. Bursts beyond policy will trigger cost-approval webhook to procurement.
- Warm caching: advise pre-warming for clinical flows and keep a small prefix cache pinned to avoid cold-start latency for critical endpoints.
- Networking: need peering and 3x 1Gbps ephemeral egress endpoints (we can increase later). See network_requirements_v1.docx for IP ranges.

If the customer is okay with the above, we can schedule capacity reservation and target a pilot activation window 10 business days after contract signature and netops coordination.

Ben
Staff Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

"Redwood will provision the Dedicated GPU pool in the customer-designated cloud region (us-east-1). Customer data processed by the Dedicated instance remains in-region and networked via VPC peering. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS keys for encryption at rest; if customer chooses Redwood-managed KMS, keys are region-scoped. Redwood will sign a BAA for HIPAA-covered workflows and provide SOC 2 Type II evidence on request."
